segments: Use Nix to build reproducible development environments for most programming languages.
Why manage development environments with Nix?

The original language examples pin nixos-24.05. Python 3.11, Go 1.21, Node 20, and the other versions shown are examples, not recommendations for currently secure versions. Choose supported toolchains and commit flake.lock; also manage the project package manager’s lockfile, external services, and runtime state.
Time-consuming setup for new team members
Reusable tool environments with pinned inputs
One-command startup for the development environment
The basic approach: nix-shell / nix run
direnv can automatically load a development environment when you enter a directory.
use flake and use nix are alternatives; do not call both for the same environment. Read .envrc and shellHook before authorizing them, because they execute code.
The environment now loads automatically when you enter the directory and unloads when you leave.

This kind of shellHook creates directories and starts background processes; exiting the devShell does not automatically stop the services. Add data directories to .gitignore and pin database major versions to avoid incompatibility with existing data directories. Use passwordless authentication only for local development.
This provides the Docker CLI; it does not automatically configure or start the host Docker daemon or grant access to its socket. Declare container services separately.

The recipes require the project’s npm scripts, Poetry configuration, and Alembic migrations to exist already. dev is an illustrative script for starting services concurrently; the project must handle cleanup on exit and port conflicts. Initialize PostgreSQL first, then start it, then create the database.
Use Flakes: pin Nix inputs; external downloads and mutable state still need to be handled
Document the setup: explain how to start the environment in the README
Support multiple platforms: support multiple systems where possible

The complete Flake example includes inputs, outputs, system, and pkgs; the Redis and Docker snippets omit the surrounding structure and must be placed inside an existing outputs scope. The empty packages list in haskellPackages.shellFor is only a skeleton: fill it with the project’s derivation. corepack manages Yarn/pnpm shims and does not provide the npm bundled with Node; check the pinned Nixpkgs to see whether the package names still exist. The database examples avoid passwordless TCP listeners; these services and development environments have not been run locally.
